description.value: The study compared egocentric and allocentric spatial orientation and memory in patients with behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia and Alzheimer’s disease and healthy controls, combining a virtual supermarket task with structural neuroimaging.

spans.text: In the current study, the virtual supermarket task was employed with a novel spatial layout component to compare egocentric and allocentric spatial processing in AD and bvFTD.

description.value: A cohort study of patients with dementia and healthy controls recruited from the Sydney frontotemporal dementia research group database.

spans.text: A cohort of 22 patients with dementia (11 bvFTD; 11 AD) and 14 healthy controls were assessed on the virtual supermarket task of spatial orientation and a battery of standardized neuropsychological measures of visual and verbal memory performance.

spans.text: Bilateral hippocampal volume was significantly reduced compared to control in bvFTD and AD patient groups (all p values <0.01) (Fig. 5). description.value: Ecological virtual supermarket spatial orientation task consisting of 14 randomized video trials. Participants viewed first-person videos involving travel to locations within a supermarket and judged heading direction and spatial location relative to the starting location using egocentric and allocentric frameworks.

instructions.value: Participants were instructed to view short videos involving movement to new supermarket locations and judge heading direction and location relative to the original starting location. One practice trial was provided.

stimuli.value: First-person virtual supermarket video trials and supermarket spatial maps.
